title: Vitamin B12 absorption requires:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Vitamin B12 absorption requires:
options: Transferrin and hydrochloric acid, with absorption in the duodenum
Intrinsic factor from gastric parietal cells, with absorption in the terminal ileum
body.explanation: Pernicious anaemia: autoantibodies against parietal cells or intrinsic factor.

title: Primary haemostasis involves:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Primary haemostasis involves:
options: Formation of a fibrin clot by the coagulation cascade
Vasoconstriction and formation of the platelet plug
body.explanation: Platelets adhere (vWF binding GPIb), become activated and aggregate (fibrinogen bridging GPIIb/IIIa).

title: A person with blood group O:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: A person with blood group O:
options: Has A and B antigens on red cells and no antibodies in plasma
Has anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma
body.explanation: Group O red cells are the universal donor cells; AB is the universal plasma donor and red-cell recipient.

title: Folate or vitamin B12 deficiency causes:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Folate or vitamin B12 deficiency causes:
options: Microcytic hypochromic anaemia with target cells and a low reticulocyte count
Megaloblastic macrocytic anaemia with hypersegmented neutrophils
body.explanation: Impaired DNA synthesis delays nuclear maturation.

title: The prothrombin time (PT/INR) mainly explores:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: The prothrombin time (PT/INR) mainly explores:
options: The extrinsic and common pathways (VII, X, V, II, fibrinogen)
The intrinsic and common pathways (VIII, IX, XI, XII, X, V, II)
body.explanation: aPTT explores the intrinsic + common pathways and is prolonged in haemophilia A and B.

title: Von Willebrand factor:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Von Willebrand factor:
options: Links platelets to exposed collagen and carries factor VIII
Is a vitamin K-dependent factor made by the liver and activated by thrombin
body.explanation: It is made by endothelial cells and megakaryocytes.

title: The main hormone that drives erythropoiesis is:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: The main hormone that drives erythropoiesis is:
options: Thrombopoietin, produced mainly by the liver
Erythropoietin, produced mainly by the kidney
body.explanation: Peritubular cells of the kidney release EPO in response to hypoxia.

title: Dietary iron is absorbed mainly in:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Dietary iron is absorbed mainly in:
options: The terminal ileum, bound to intrinsic factor
body.explanation: Absorption is regulated by hepcidin, which blocks ferroportin. Vitamin B12 is absorbed in the terminal ileum.

title: The vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors are:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: The vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors are:
options: II, VII, IX, X (and proteins C and S)
body.explanation: Warfarin blocks their γ-carboxylation.

title: The normal life span of a red blood cell is about:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: The normal life span of a red blood cell is about:
body.explanation: Old red cells are removed by macrophages, mainly in the spleen.

title: The most abundant white blood cell in adult blood is:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: The most abundant white blood cell in adult blood is:
body.explanation: Neutrophils ≈ 50-70%, lymphocytes ≈ 20-40%.

title: In adults, haematopoiesis normally takes place in:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: In adults, haematopoiesis normally takes place in:
options: The red bone marrow of the axial skeleton and proximal long bones
The liver and spleen, as in the fetus from the third month
body.explanation: Yolk sac → liver/spleen → bone marrow; in adults it is restricted to flat bones, vertebrae and proximal femur and humerus.

title: Haemophilia A is due to a deficiency of:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Haemophilia A is due to a deficiency of:
body.explanation: X-linked recessive; haemophilia B = factor IX.

title: Eosinophilia is classically seen in:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Eosinophilia is classically seen in:
options: Bacterial pneumonia and other acute bacterial infections
body.explanation: Eosinophils fight helminths and take part in allergic reactions.

title: Thrombocytopenia is defined as a platelet count below:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Thrombocytopenia is defined as a platelet count below:
body.explanation: Normal range ≈ 150-400 × 10⁹/L; spontaneous bleeding usually appears well below 20-30 × 10⁹/L.

title: A high reticulocyte count in an anaemic patient suggests:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: A high reticulocyte count in an anaemic patient suggests:
options: Haemolysis or acute blood loss (regenerative anaemia)
Bone marrow failure or aplasia (central anaemia)
body.explanation: The marrow responds normally by releasing young red cells.

title: The best single test to confirm iron deficiency is:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: The best single test to confirm iron deficiency is:
options: Serum iron (low) measured in the morning
body.explanation: Low ferritin reflects depleted stores; ferritin rises with inflammation, so it can be falsely normal.

title: A microcytic anaemia (low MCV) is typical of:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: A microcytic anaemia (low MCV) is typical of:
body.explanation: Microcytic: iron deficiency, thalassaemia, anaemia of chronic disease (sometimes), sideroblastic anaemia.

title: Splenomegaly can cause:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Splenomegaly can cause:
options: A raised platelet count in all cases, with thrombosis and iron overload
Hypersplenism with cytopenias (pooling and destruction of blood cells)
body.explanation: An enlarged spleen sequesters platelets and red cells.

title: Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) is:
subject: subj:hemato1

body.stem: Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) is:
body.explanation: MCV = Hct / RBC (normal ≈ 80-100 fL); MCH = Hb / RBC; MCHC = Hb / Hct.
